messages:
sam_support: FYI incoming from Acme EU — they see a spike in latency (~200-400ms) and intermittent 401s. Customer says traffic is routing to a US pop even though users are in London. Repro steps and curl attached. Can someone triage?

customer_jones: We noticed this around 10:15 UTC. Repro steps we ran: curl -v against the API from a UK office. Headers show X-Redwood-Pop: us-west-1. Also intermittently got 401 with auth token that works when routed to eu-west. Snippet:

```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: redwood-edge
X-Redwood-Pop: us-west-1
...
# then some requests
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "token_expired"
}
```

We also did a dig from the customer network:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
us-pop-1.redwood.ai.
# TTL 3600
```

boris_sre: thanks — two quick angles: 1) resolver/ISP might be returning a CNAME that points at a US anycast hostname (CNAME rotation / weighted records), 2) EDNS/Client-Subnet stripping by ISP can make us pick the wrong pop. Can you paste the full dig +trace and the resolver IP used by the client (eg the answer from dig @resolver +short CHAINS)?

maria_network: Also check whether the client network is stuck on an old resolver cache that saw a previous rotation. If the CNAME changed recently and TTLs are long, some resolvers will keep pointing to the old variant (which resolves to a US pop).

customer_jones: paste of dig +trace and resolver IP:
```
$ dig +trace api.redwood.ai
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 54123
api.redwood.ai. 3600 IN CNAME weighted-eu-us.redwood.ai.
weighted-eu-us.redwood.ai. 3600 IN CNAME us-pop-1.redwood.ai.
us-pop-1.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 3.120.45.67
;; Query time: 22 msec

Resolver seen in request headers: 203.0.113.45 (ISP-X resolver)
```

customer_jones: Note we only started seeing the US CNAME target after a config change this morning (rolling weighted CNAME update), but users in London should still be pinned to eu by policy.

boris_sre: That resolver IP is in ISP-X's pool; they have been reported to strip EDNS/CLIENT-SUBNET in the past. Without ECS, our authoritative sees the resolver IP (often in the US path) and can return a US-optimized target. Two possible causes: the resolver is returning a stale cached CNAME chain that ends up at the US target, or our geoip mapping on the control plane returned the wrong region for that resolver because of an out-of-date geoip file.

maria_network: Quick repro commands to try on their side: 
1) dig @203.0.113.45 api.redwood.ai +short +ttlid
2) dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short +ttlid
3) curl -H "Edns-Client-Subnet: 2.16.0.0/13" -v to see whether responses change
Also ask them to flush the resolver cache or switch their local DNS to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 to see if the mapping flips back to eu.

lucy_ps: Customer impact: they alerted about increased token costs and user-facing latency. Billing question from the account team: if this was caused by a routing/regional misroute, do we need to consider crediting the customer? Need SRE root cause first but flagging for finance. :warning:

boris_sre: I'm going to check our geoip rollout logs and the control plane mapping for that resolver IP. If the geoip DB rolled out recently and some edges didn't refresh, you'd see inconsistent answers. Also creating an internal incident: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-314 (added acme-eu).

deploy-bot: geoip-db rollout (2026-03-10T09:40:03Z) -> success on 95% edges, 5% pending.

boris_sre: OK the rollout note explains the window — a small fraction of edges had the old mapping which preferred US. For the immediate mitigation I can: 1) push a targeted purge for the resolver IP on our edge caches, 2) add an exception in routing policy for account acme-eu to prefer eu-pop for 1 hour.

sam_support: Please coordinate with @maria_network for the purge and let the customer know the temporary fallback. Ask them to try switching to 1.1.1.1 and report latency and headers.

maria_network: Purge command I ran (internal): 
```
edgectl purge-dns --resolver 203.0.113.45 --name api.redwood.ai --force
```
Ran it against the affected edges; status: queued -> done. Also applied route override for acme-eu account. Monitor logs for hits to us-pop-1.

customer_jones: switching to 1.1.1.1 for DNS now. Quick test shows X-Redwood-Pop: eu-west-1 and latency back to ~60ms. Thanks — will watch for 30 mins and report.

lucy_ps: noted. I'll hold off on billing actions until we have stable routing for 1h and SRE confirmation.

boris_sre: Follow-up: we'll keep this incident open for 1h to monitor. Action items: 1) ask ISP-X to stop stripping ECS (we'll provide packet sample), 2) evaluate reducing TTLs for weighted CNAMEs during future rotations, 3) add a guardrail to route-by-account if geoip rollout is partial.

sam_support: closing loop for now — customer confirmed recovered after DNS switch and purge. Will reopen if any recurrence. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
